The idea of the fox costume had been suggested to him by [Paul Conroy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Conroy_(music_executive) "Paul Conroy (music executive)") and Glen Colson, employees of Genesis's record label, [Charisma Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charisma_Records "Charisma Records").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGiammetti2020155%E2%80%93157-36) Gabriel said he consulted the rest of Genesis about the fox costume but grew tired of arguing about it, but the other members all maintained that nothing was said about it beforehand and that when Gabriel came out in costume they initially mistook him for a fan invading the stage.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGiammetti2020157,_162-37) The incident received front-page coverage in _Melody Maker_, giving them national exposure which allowed the group to double their performance fee.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] One of Gabriel's stories was printed on the liner notes of their live album, _[Genesis Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genesis\_Live "Genesis Live")_ (1973). By late 1973, following the success of _[Selling England by the Pound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Selling\_England\_by\_the\_Pound "Selling England by the Pound")_ (1973), which centred on English themes and literary and materialistic references, a typical Genesis show had Gabriel wear fluorescent make-up, a cape, and bat wings for "[Watcher of the Skies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watcher_of_the_Skies "Watcher of the Skies")", a helmet, chest plate, and a shield for "[Dancing with the Moonlit Knight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dancing_with_the_Moonlit_Knight "Dancing with the Moonlit Knight")", a [crown of thorns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crown_of_thorns "Crown of thorns") and a flower mask for "[Supper's Ready](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supper's_Ready "Supper's Ready")", and an old man mask for "The Musical Box".[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGiammetti2020162,_203-38)

Gabriel continued to fight for involvement with Genesis's keyboards throughout his time with the group, and following a lengthy argument with Banks, he was allowed to play a minor keyboard part on "[I Know What I Like (In Your Wardrobe)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Know_What_I_Like_(In_Your_Wardrobe) "I Know What I Like (In Your Wardrobe)")", only for this part to be left out of the mix.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGiammetti2020197-39) "I Know What I Like" became Genesis's first hit single, reaching number 21 in the [UK Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Singles_Chart "UK Singles Chart").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-40)

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c9/Peter_Gabriel%2C_April_1975.jpg/250px-Peter_Gabriel%2C_April_1975.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Peter_Gabriel,_April_1975.jpg)

Gabriel performing during [The Lamb Lies Down on Broadway Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Lamb_Lies_Down_on_Broadway_Tour "The Lamb Lies Down on Broadway Tour"), 1975

_[The Lamb Lies Down on Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lamb\_Lies\_Down\_on\_Broadway "The Lamb Lies Down on Broadway")_ (1974) was Gabriel's final studio album with Genesis. He devised its story of the spiritual journey of Rael, a Puerto Rican youth living in New York City, and insisted upon writing all the lyrics himself, whereas on previous albums the lyrics had been divided among all the members of Genesis.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGiammetti2020211%E2%80%93213-41) Tensions increased during this period, and Gabriel split with the band to pursue a film project with [William Friedkin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Friedkin "William Friedkin"), only to rejoin a week later.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-Mike_on_Mike-25) Matters were complicated further with the difficult birth of Gabriel's first daughter, resulting in periods of time away from the band. The other members complained that Gabriel was showing a lack of commitment to the band. Gabriel saw this as a "really unsympathetic handling of my dealing with a family crisis" and said it caused a breakdown in his relationships with the rest of Genesis; Rutherford later admitted that they had been overly fixated on their music and were very unhelpful in what must have been a difficult time for Gabriel.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGiammetti2020217%E2%80%93218-42) Gabriel was late to deliver the lyrics, but has denied that he was too busy to write much music for the album and relied on contributions from Banks and Rutherford.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGiammetti2020236-43) Banks corroborated that Gabriel was the primary composer of the _Lamb_ songs "[The Carpet Crawlers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Carpet_Crawlers "The Carpet Crawlers")" and "The Chamber of 32 Doors" and the sole composer of "Counting Out Time".[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGiammetti2020225%E2%80%93228-44)

During a stop in Cleveland, Ohio, early into the album's tour, Gabriel informed the band of his intention to leave at its conclusion.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGenesis2007158-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-46) Rutherford recalled that they all "could see it coming".[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-Mike_on_Mike-25) Music critics often focused their reviews on Gabriel's theatrics and took the band's musical performance as secondary, which irritated the rest of the band.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBowlerDray199293-47) The tour ended in May 1975, after which Gabriel wrote a piece for the press on 15 August, entitled "Out, Angels Out", about his departure, his disillusion with the business, and his desire to spend time with his family.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBowlerDray1992107-48) The news stunned fans of the group and left commentators wondering if the band could survive without him.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-Leaves_Genesis-49)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-Reunion-50) His exit resulted in drummer [Phil Collins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phil_Collins "Phil Collins") reluctantly taking over on lead vocals after 400 singers were fruitlessly auditioned.

### 1975–1985: Solo debut with four self-titled albums

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Peter_Gabriel&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 1975–1985: Solo debut with four self-titled albums")]

Gabriel described his break from the music business as his "learning period", during which he took piano and music lessons. He had recorded demos by the end of 1975, the fruits of a period of writing around 20 songs with his friend Martin Hall.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-MM751206-51) In 1977, Gabriel released his solo debut, _[Peter Gabriel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter\_Gabriel\_(1977\_album) "Peter Gabriel (1977 album)")_, which was recorded in Toronto with [Bob Ezrin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Ezrin "Bob Ezrin") serving as the album's producer.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-52) Gabriel did not title his first four studio albums. All were labelled _Peter Gabriel_, using the same typeface, with designs by [Hipgnosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hipgnosis "Hipgnosis"). "The idea is to do it like a magazine, which will only come out once a year," he remarked in 1978. "So it's the same title, the same lettering in the same place; only the photo is different."[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-53)

_Peter Gabriel_ (a.k.a. _Peter Gabriel 1: Car_) was released in February 1977 and reached No. 7 in the UK and No. 38 in the US. Its [lead single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lead_single "Lead single"), "[Solsbury Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solsbury_Hill_(song) "Solsbury Hill (song)")", is an autobiographical song about a spiritual experience on top of [Solsbury Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solsbury_Hill "Solsbury Hill") in Somerset. "It's about being prepared to lose what you have for what you might get..." said Gabriel. "It's about letting go."[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-FOOTNOTEEaslea2018203-54) Gabriel toured the album with an 80-date tour from March to November 1977 with a band that included guitarist [Robert Fripp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Fripp "Robert Fripp") of [King Crimson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Crimson "King Crimson") often playing off stage and introduced as "Dusty Rhodes".[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-Lamb-55)

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/81/Peter_gabriel_31081978_02_400.jpg/250px-Peter_gabriel_31081978_02_400.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Peter_gabriel_31081978_02_400.jpg)

Gabriel onstage in 1978

In late 1977, Gabriel started recording the [second _Peter Gabriel_ studio album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel_(1978_album) "Peter Gabriel (1978 album)") (a.k.a. _Peter Gabriel 2: Scratch_) in the Netherlands, with Fripp as producer. Its "Mother of Violence" was written by Gabriel and his first wife Jill. Released in June 1978, the album went to No. 10 in the UK and No. 45 in the US. Gabriel's tour for the album lasted from August to December 1978. On this tour, Gabriel and his band shaved their heads.

Gabriel recorded the [third _Peter Gabriel_ studio album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel_(1980_album) "Peter Gabriel (1980 album)") (a.k.a. _Peter Gabriel 3: Melt_) in England in 1979. He developed an interest in African music and [drum machines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drum_machine "Drum machine") and later hailed the record as his artistic breakthrough. Gabriel banned the use of cymbals on the album to grant more sonic space for instruments like keyboards and synths. This resulted in the creation of the distinctive [gated reverb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gated_reverb "Gated reverb"),[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-56) an audio processing technique which came about while recording drums on "[Intruder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intruder_(song) "Intruder (song)")", one of the tracks featuring [Phil Collins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phil_Collins "Phil Collins"). Collins implemented the reverb technique to great effect on his debut solo single "[In the Air Tonight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_the_Air_Tonight "In the Air Tonight")" and it later became a signature sound of the 1980s and beyond.

Upon completion [Atlantic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Records "Atlantic Records"), Gabriel's US distributor who had released his first two albums, refused to put out _Peter Gabriel 3: Melt_ as they thought it was not commercial enough. Gabriel signed a recording contract with [Mercury Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercury_Records "Mercury Records").[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-Rolling_Stone_1987-10-29-57) Released in May 1980, the album went to No. 1 in the UK for three weeks. In the US, it peaked at No. 22. The single "[Games Without Frontiers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Games_Without_Frontiers_(song) "Games Without Frontiers (song)")" went to No. 4 and "[Biko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biko_(song) "Biko (song)")" went to No. 36 in the UK. After a handful of shows in 1979, Gabriel toured the album from February to October 1980. The tour marked Gabriel's first successful instance of [crowd surfing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowd_surfing "Crowd surfing") (following his failed June 1971 attempt when touring with Genesis) when he fell back into the audience in a crucifix position. The stunt became a staple of his live shows.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-Rolling_Stone_1987-10-29-57)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-58)

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c9/Peter_Gabriel_19800906.jpg/250px-Peter_Gabriel_19800906.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Peter_Gabriel_19800906.jpg)

Gabriel performing in 1980

On [_Peter Gabriel_ four](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel_(1982_album) "Peter Gabriel (1982 album)") (a.k.a. _Peter Gabriel 4: Security_), Gabriel took on greater responsibility over the production than before. He recorded it in 1981 and 1982, solely on digital tape, with a mobile studio parked at his home, [Ashcombe House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashcombe_House,_Somerset "Ashcombe House, Somerset"), in Somerset. Gabriel used a [Fairlight CMI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairlight_CMI "Fairlight CMI") digital [sampling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sampler_(musical_instrument) "Sampler (musical instrument)") synthesiser and incorporated electronic instrumentation with sampling world beat percussion. "Over the course of the last two albums," he observed, "I've got back into a rhythm consciousness. And the writing—particularly with the invention of these drum machines—is fantastic. You can store in their memories rhythms that interest you and excite you. And then the groove will carry on without you, and the groove will be exactly what you want it to be, rather than what a drummer thinks is appropriate for what you're doing."[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-White_Shadow_pp12-21)

The fourth _Peter Gabriel_, released in September 1982, hit No. 6 in the UK and No. 28 in the US. The second single, "[Shock the Monkey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shock_the_Monkey "Shock the Monkey")", became Gabriel's first top 40 hit in the US, reaching No. 29. To handle American distribution, Gabriel signed with [Geffen Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geffen_Records "Geffen Records"), which—initially unbeknown to Gabriel—titled the album _Security_ to differentiate it from the first three. Gabriel's 1982 tour lasted a year and became his first to make a profit.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-Musician_1986-07-59) Recordings from the tour were released on Gabriel's debut live release, _[Plays Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plays\_Live "Plays Live")_ (1983).

Gabriel produced versions of the third and fourth _Peter Gabriel_ albums with German lyrics. The third consisted of the studio recordings, overdubbed with new vocals. The fourth was remixed, with several tracks extended or altered. In 1983, Gabriel developed the soundtrack for [Alan Parker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Parker "Alan Parker")'s drama film _[Birdy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birdy\_(film) "Birdy (film)")_ (1984), co-produced with [Daniel Lanois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Lanois "Daniel Lanois"). This consisted of new material, without lyrics, as well as remixed instrumentals from his previous studio album.

### 1985–1997: _So_ and _Us_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Peter_Gabriel&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 1985–1997: So and Us")]

After finishing the soundtrack to _Birdy_, Gabriel shifted his musical focus from rhythm and texture, as heard on _Peter Gabriel_ four and _Birdy_, towards more straightforward songs.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-Musician_1986-07-59) In 1985, he recorded his fifth studio album, _[So](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/So\_(album) "So (album)")_ (also co-produced with Lanois).[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-60)_So_ was released in May 1986 and reached No. 1 in the UK and No. 2 in the US. It remains Gabriel's best-selling album with over five million copies sold in the US alone.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-BPI-61)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-RIAA-62) It produced "[In Your Eyes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_Your_Eyes_(Peter_Gabriel_song) "In Your Eyes (Peter Gabriel song)")", one of Gabriel's signature songs that has become a concert staple; the song includes a distinctive vocal appearance by [Youssou N'Dour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Youssou_N'Dour "Youssou N'Dour"). _So_ also included three UK top 20 singles: "[Sledgehammer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sledgehammer_(Peter_Gabriel_song) "Sledgehammer (Peter Gabriel song)")", "[Big Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Time_(Peter_Gabriel_song) "Big Time (Peter Gabriel song)")", and "[Don't Give Up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_Give_Up_(Peter_Gabriel_and_Kate_Bush_song) "Don't Give Up (Peter Gabriel and Kate Bush song)")", a duet with [Kate Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Bush "Kate Bush").[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-UKCharts-63)

The first went to No. 1 on the US [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"), Gabriel's only single of his career to do so. It knocked "[Invisible Touch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invisible_Touch_(song) "Invisible Touch (song)")" by Genesis, his former band, out of the top spot, which was also their only US number one hit. In the UK, the single went to No. 4.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-Billboard-64) In 1990, _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ ranked _So_ at No. 14 on its list of "Top 100 Albums of the Eighties".[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-65)

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/98/Peter_Gabriel-Conspiracy_of_Hope-by_Steven_Toole.jpg/250px-Peter_Gabriel-Conspiracy_of_Hope-by_Steven_Toole.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Peter_Gabriel-Conspiracy_of_Hope-by_Steven_Toole.jpg)

Gabriel performing in 1986

"Sledgehammer" was particularly successful, dealing with sex and sexual relations through lyrical innuendos. Its famed music video was a collaboration between director [Stephen R. Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_R._Johnson "Stephen R. Johnson"), [Aardman Animations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aardman_Animations "Aardman Animations"),[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-Time-2) and the [Brothers Quay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brothers_Quay "Brothers Quay") and won a record nine [MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Awards "MTV Video Music Awards") in 1987.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-Time-2) In 1998, it was named MTV's number one animated video of all time.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-66)_So_ earned Gabriel two wins at the [1987](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_BRIT_Awards_ceremonies#1987 "List of BRIT Awards ceremonies")[Brit Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brit_Awards "Brit Awards") for Best British Male Solo Artist and Best British Video (for "Sledgehammer").[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-BritAwards-67) He was nominated for four [Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Awards "Grammy Awards"): [Best Male Rock Vocal Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Male_Rock_Vocal_Performance "Grammy Award for Best Male Rock Vocal Performance"), [Song of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Song_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Song of the Year"), and [Record of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Record_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Record of the Year") for "Sledgehammer", and [Album of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Album of the Year") for _So_.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-68) Gabriel toured worldwide to support _So_ with the This Way Up Tour, from November 1986 to October 1987.

In 1988, Gabriel became involved as composer for [Martin Scorsese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Scorsese "Martin Scorsese")'s film _[The Last Temptation of Christ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Last\_Temptation\_of\_Christ\_(film) "The Last Temptation of Christ (film)")_ (1988). Scorsese had contacted Gabriel about the project since 1983 and wished, according to Gabriel, to present "the struggle between the humanity and divinity of Christ in a powerful and original way".[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-UCR15-69) Gabriel used musicians from [WOMAD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_of_Music,_Arts_and_Dance "World of Music, Arts and Dance") to perform instrumental pieces with focus on rhythm and African, Middle Eastern and European textures, using the [National Sound Archive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Library_Sound_Archive "British Library Sound Archive") in London for additional inspiration.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-UCR15-69) The initial plan had dedicated ten weeks for recording before it was cut to three, leaving Gabriel unable to finish all the pieces he originally wanted to record.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-UCR15-69) When the film was finished, Gabriel worked on the soundtrack for an additional four months to develop more of his unfinished ideas. Its soundtrack was released as _[Passion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passion\_(Peter\_Gabriel\_album) "Passion (Peter Gabriel album)")_ in June 1989. It won Gabriel a [Grammy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award "Grammy Award") for [Best New Age Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_New_Age_Album "Grammy Award for Best New Age Album") and a nomination for a [Golden Globe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Awards "Golden Globe Awards") for [Best Original Score – Motion Picture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Original_Score "Golden Globe Award for Best Original Score"). In 1990, Gabriel put out his first compilation album, _[Shaking the Tree: Sixteen Golden Greats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaking\_the\_Tree:\_Sixteen\_Golden\_Greats "Shaking the Tree: Sixteen Golden Greats")_, which sold 2 million copies in the US.

Up until 1989, Gabriel was managed by [Gail Colson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gail_Colson "Gail Colson").[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-Perrone-70) From 1989 to 1992, Gabriel recorded his follow-up to _So_, titled _[Us](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Us\_(Peter\_Gabriel\_album) "Us (Peter Gabriel album)")_. The album saw Gabriel address personal themes, including his failed first marriage, psychotherapy, and the growing distance between him and his eldest daughter at the time.

Gabriel's introspection within the context of the album _Us_ can be seen in the first single release "[Digging in the Dirt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digging_in_the_Dirt "Digging in the Dirt")" directed by John Downer. Accompanied by a video featuring Gabriel covered in snails and various foliage, this song made reference to the psychotherapy which had taken up much of Gabriel's time since the previous studio album. Gabriel describes his struggle to get through to his daughter in "[Come Talk to Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Talk_to_Me "Come Talk to Me")" directed by [Matt Mahurin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Mahurin "Matt Mahurin"), which featured backing vocals by [Sinéad O'Connor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sin%C3%A9ad_O'Connor "Sinéad O'Connor"). O'Connor also lent vocals to "[Blood of Eden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_of_Eden "Blood of Eden")", directed by [Nichola Bruce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nichola_Bruce "Nichola Bruce") and Michael Coulson, the third single to be released from the album, and once again dealing with relationship struggles, this time going right back to [Adam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam "Adam")'s rib for inspiration.

The album is one of Gabriel's most personal. It met with less success than _So_, reaching No. 2 in the album chart on both sides of the Atlantic, and making modest chart impact with the singles "Digging in the Dirt" and the funkier "[Steam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steam_(Peter_Gabriel_song) "Steam (Peter Gabriel song)")", which evoked memories of "Sledgehammer". Gabriel followed the release of the album with the [Secret World Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_World_Tour "Secret World Tour"), first using touring keyboardist Joy Askew to sing O'Connor's part, then O'Connor herself for a few months.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-Zindler1999-71) O'Connor quit the tour, and was replaced by [Paula Cole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Cole "Paula Cole"), the latter appearing on the tour recordings: a double album _[Secret World Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret\_World\_Live "Secret World Live")_, and a concert video also called _[Secret World Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret\_World\_Live\_(film) "Secret World Live (film)")_, both released in 1994.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-72) The film received the 1996 [Grammy Award for Best Long Form Music Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Long_Form_Music_Video "Grammy Award for Best Long Form Music Video"), naming director Francois Girard and producer Robert Warr.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-73)

Gabriel employed an innovative approach in the marketing of the _Us_ album. Not wishing to feature only images of himself, he asked artist filmmakers [Nichola Bruce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nichola_Bruce "Nichola Bruce") and Michael Coulson to co-ordinate a marketing campaign using contemporary artists. Artists such as [Helen Chadwick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helen_Chadwick "Helen Chadwick"), [Rebecca Horn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebecca_Horn "Rebecca Horn"), [Nils-Udo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nils-Udo "Nils-Udo"), [Andy Goldsworthy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Goldsworthy "Andy Goldsworthy"), [David Mach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Mach "David Mach") and [Yayoi Kusama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yayoi_Kusama "Yayoi Kusama") collaborated to create original artworks for each song on the multi-million-selling CD. Coulson and Bruce documented the process on Hi-8 video. Bruce left Real World and Coulson continued with the campaign, using the documentary background material as the basis for a promotional EPK, the long-form video _All About Us_ and the interactive CD-ROM _[Xplora1: Peter Gabriel's Secret World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xplora1:\_Peter\_Gabriel's\_Secret\_World "Xplora1: Peter Gabriel's Secret World")_.

Gabriel won three more [Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Awards "Grammy Awards"), all in the Music Video category. He won the [Grammy Award for Best Short Form Music Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Music_Video "Grammy Award for Best Music Video") in 1993 and 1994 for the videos to "Digging in the Dirt" and "Steam", respectively. Gabriel also won the 1996 [Grammy Award for Best Long Form Music Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Music_Video "Grammy Award for Best Music Video") for his _[Secret World Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret\_World\_Live\_(DVD) "Secret World Live (DVD)")_ video.

### 1997–2009: _OVO_ and _Up_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Peter_Gabriel&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 1997–2009: OVO and Up")]

In 1997, Gabriel was invited to participate in the direction and soundtrack of the [Millennium Dome Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millennium_Dome_Show "Millennium Dome Show"), a live multimedia performance staged in the [Millennium Dome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millennium_Dome "Millennium Dome") in London throughout 2000.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-74) Gabriel said the team were given free rein, which contributed to the various problems they encountered with it, such as a lack of proper budgeting. He also felt that management, while succeeding to get the building finished on time, failed to understand the artistic side of the show and its content.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-TT00-75) Gabriel's soundtrack was released as _[OVO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OVO\_(album) "OVO (album)")_ in June 2000. [The Story of OVO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Story_of_OVO "The Story of OVO") was released in the CD-booklet-shaped comic book which was part of the CD edition with the title "OVO The Millennium Show".[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-TheStoryOfOVO-76) As part of Record Store Day 2025, OVO celebrated its 25th anniversary and was released on vinyl for the first time in limited quantity.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-77)

Around that same time, the Genesis greatest hits album, _[Turn It On Again: The Hits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turn\_It\_On\_Again:\_The\_Hits "Turn It On Again: The Hits")_ (1999), featured Gabriel sharing vocals with [Phil Collins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phil_Collins "Phil Collins") on a new version of "[The Carpet Crawlers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Carpet_Crawlers "The Carpet Crawlers")" entitled "The Carpet Crawlers 1999", produced by [Trevor Horn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Horn "Trevor Horn"). In 2002 he stuck with soundtrack work for his next project, scoring for the Australian film _[Rabbit-Proof Fence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rabbit-Proof\_Fence "Rabbit-Proof Fence")_ (2002) with [worldbeat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Worldbeat "Worldbeat") music. Released in June 2002, _[Long Walk Home: Music from the Rabbit-Proof Fence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long\_Walk\_Home:\_Music\_from\_the\_Rabbit-Proof\_Fence "Long Walk Home: Music from the Rabbit-Proof Fence")_ received a Golden Globe Award nomination for Best Original Score – Motion Picture.

Later in 2002, _[Up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Up\_(Peter\_Gabriel\_album) "Up (Peter Gabriel album)")_, Gabriel's first full-length studio album in a decade, was released in September 2002. He started work on it in 1995 before production halted three years later to focus time on other projects and collaborations. Work resumed in 2000, by which time Gabriel had 130 potential songs for the album, and spent almost two years on it before management at [Virgin Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virgin_Records "Virgin Records") pushed Gabriel to complete it.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-TG02-78)_Up_ reached No. 9 in the US and No. 11 in the UK, and supported with a world tour with a band that included Gabriel's daughter Melanie on backing vocals. The tour was documented with two live DVDs: _[Growing Up Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Growing\_Up\_Live "Growing Up Live")_ (2003) and _[Still Growing Up: Live & Unwrapped](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Still\_Growing\_Up:\_Live\_&\_Unwrapped "Still Growing Up: Live & Unwrapped")_ (2005).

In 2004, Gabriel met with his former Genesis bandmates to discuss the possibility of staging _[The Lamb Lies Down on Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lamb\_Lies\_Down\_on\_Broadway "The Lamb Lies Down on Broadway")_ (1974) as a reunion tour. He ultimately dismissed the idea, paving the way for Banks, Rutherford and Collins to organise the [Turn It On Again: The Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turn_It_On_Again:_The_Tour "Turn It On Again: The Tour"). Gabriel produced and performed at the [Eden Project Live 8 concert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_8_concert,_Eden_Project "Live 8 concert, Eden Project") in July 2005. He joined [Cat Stevens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cat_Stevens "Cat Stevens") on stage to perform "[Wild World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wild_World_(song) "Wild World (song)")" during [Nelson Mandela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Mandela "Nelson Mandela")'s [46664](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/46664_(concerts) "46664 (concerts)") concert. In 2005, [FIFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA "FIFA") asked Gabriel and Brian Eno to organise an opening ceremony for the [2006 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_FIFA_World_Cup "2006 FIFA World Cup") in Germany, but FIFA cancelled the idea in January 2006. At the opening ceremony of the [2006 Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_Winter_Olympics "2006 Winter Olympics") in [Turin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turin "Turin"), Gabriel performed [John Lennon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Lennon "John Lennon")'s "[Imagine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imagine_(John_Lennon_song) "Imagine (John Lennon song)")".[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-79)

In November 2006, the Seventh World Summit of [Nobel Peace Laureates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Peace_Laureate "Nobel Peace Laureate") in Rome presented Gabriel with the [Man of Peace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Man_of_Peace "Man of Peace") award. The award, presented by former General Secretary of the USSR and Nobel Peace Prize winner [Mikhail Gorbachev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mikhail_Gorbachev "Mikhail Gorbachev") and [Walter Veltroni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Veltroni "Walter Veltroni"), Mayor of Rome, was an acknowledgement of Gabriel's extensive contribution and work on behalf of human rights and peace. The award was presented in the Giulio Cesare Hall of the Campidoglio in Rome. At the end of the year, he was awarded the _[Q](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Q\_(magazine) "Q (magazine)")_ magazine Lifetime Achievement Award, presented to him by American musician [Moby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moby "Moby"). In an interview published in the magazine to accompany the award, Gabriel's contribution to music was described as "vast and enduring".

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c2/Peter_Gabriel_BBC_Radio_2_2007.jpg/250px-Peter_Gabriel_BBC_Radio_2_2007.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Peter_Gabriel_BBC_Radio_2_2007.jpg)

Gabriel at the 2007 [BBC Radio 2 Folk Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Radio_2_Folk_Awards "BBC Radio 2 Folk Awards")

Gabriel took on a project with the [BBC World Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_World_Service "BBC World Service")'s competition "The Next Big Thing" to find the world's best young band. Gabriel judged the final six young artists with [William Orbit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Orbit "William Orbit"), [Geoff Travis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoff_Travis "Geoff Travis") and [Angélique Kidjo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang%C3%A9lique_Kidjo "Angélique Kidjo"). In June 2008, Gabriel released _[Big Blue Ball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big\_Blue\_Ball "Big Blue Ball")_, an album of various artists collaborating with each other at his Real World Studios across three summers in the 1990s. He planned its release in the US without assistance from a label; he raised £2 million towards the recording and distribution of the album with [Ingenious Media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingenious_Media "Ingenious Media") with the worldwide release handled through [Warner Bros. Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros._Records "Warner Bros. Records").[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-80) Gabriel appeared on a nationwide tour for the album in 2009.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-81) Gabriel was a judge for the 6th and 8th annual Independent Music Awards to support independent artists.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-82)

Gabriel contributed to the [Pixar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pixar "Pixar") film _[WALL-E](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WALL-E "WALL-E")_ soundtrack in 2008 with [Thomas Newman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Newman "Thomas Newman"), including the film's closing song, "[Down to Earth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Down_to_Earth_(Peter_Gabriel_song) "Down to Earth (Peter Gabriel song)")", for which they received the [Grammy Award for Best Song Written for a Motion Picture, Television or Other Visual Media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Song_Written_for_Visual_Media "Grammy Award for Best Song Written for Visual Media"). The song was also nominated for a [Golden Globe Award for Best Original Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Original_Song "Golden Globe Award for Best Original Song") and an [Academy Award for Best Original Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Original_Song "Academy Award for Best Original Song"). In February 2009, Gabriel announced that he would not be performing on the [2008 Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Academy_Awards "81st Academy Awards") telecast because producers of the show were limiting his performance of "Down to Earth" from _WALL-E_ to 90 seconds. According to Gabriel, his window was reduced to 65 seconds. [John Legend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Legend "John Legend") and the [Soweto Gospel Choir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soweto_Gospel_Choir "Soweto Gospel Choir") performed the song in his stead.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-83)

Gabriel's 2009 tour appearances included Mexico, Argentina, Chile, Peru and Venezuela. His first ever performance in Peru was held in Lima on 20 March 2009, during his second visit to the country. On 25 July 2009, he played at WOMAD Charlton Park, his only European performance of the year, to promote Witness. The show included two tracks from the then-forthcoming _[Scratch My Back](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scratch\_My\_Back "Scratch My Back")_: [Paul Simon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Simon "Paul Simon")'s "The Boy in the Bubble" and [the Magnetic Fields](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Magnetic_Fields "The Magnetic Fields")' "The Book of Love".[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-84)

### 2009–2019: _Scratch My Back_, _New Blood_ and further side projects

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Peter_Gabriel&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2009–2019: Scratch My Back, New Blood and further side projects")]

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/54/Peter-Gabriel-2011I2.jpg/250px-Peter-Gabriel-2011I2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Peter-Gabriel-2011I2.jpg)

Gabriel performing at the 2011 Skoll Awards

In 2009, Gabriel recorded _[Scratch My Back](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scratch\_My\_Back "Scratch My Back")_, an album of cover songs by various artists including [David Bowie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Bowie "David Bowie"), [Lou Reed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lou_Reed "Lou Reed"), [Arcade Fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcade_Fire "Arcade Fire"), [Radiohead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radiohead "Radiohead"), [Regina Spektor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regina_Spektor "Regina Spektor") and [Neil Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Young "Neil Young"). The original concept was for Gabriel to cover an artists' song if they, in turn, covered one of his for an album simultaneously released as _I'll Scratch Yours_, but several participants later declined or were late to deliver and it was placed on hold.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-telegraph.co.uk-85) Gabriel avoided using drums and guitar in favour of orchestral arrangements, and altered his usual songwriting method by finishing the vocals first and then the song, for which he collaborated with [John Metcalfe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Metcalfe_(composer) "John Metcalfe (composer)").[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-NYT10-86) Released in February 2010, _Scratch My Back_ reached No. 12 in the UK.

In March 2010, Gabriel was inducted into the [Rock and Roll Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame "Rock and Roll Hall of Fame") as a member of Genesis.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-87) He toured worldwide with the New Blood Tour from March 2010 to July 2012 with a 54-piece orchestra, and his daughter Melanie and Norwegian singer-songwriter [Ane Brun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ane_Brun "Ane Brun") on backing vocals. The follow-up, _[And I'll Scratch Yours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/And\_I'll\_Scratch\_Yours "And I'll Scratch Yours")_, was released in September 2013. During the New Blood Tour, Gabriel decided to expand on the _Scratch My Back_ concept and, with Metcalfe's assistance, re-record a collection of his own songs with an orchestra. The result, _[New Blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_Blood\_(Peter\_Gabriel\_album) "New Blood (Peter Gabriel album)")_, was released in October 2011.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-Q11-88)

In September 2012, Gabriel kicked off his [Back to Front Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Back_to_Front_Tour "Back to Front Tour") which featured _So_ (1986) performed in its entirety with the original musicians who played on the album, to mark its 25th anniversary.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-89) When the opening leg finished a month later, Gabriel took one year off to travel the world with his children.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-TG12-90)[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-91) The tour resumed with a European leg from September 2013 to December 2014.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-92)

In April 2014, Gabriel was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame as a solo artist by [Coldplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coldplay "Coldplay") frontman [Chris Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Martin "Chris Martin").[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-93) They performed Gabriel's "Washing of the Water" together. Gabriel performed "['Heroes'](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%22Heroes%22_(David_Bowie_song) "\"Heroes\" (David Bowie song)")" by [David Bowie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Bowie "David Bowie") with an orchestra at a concert in Berlin to commemorate the 25th anniversary of the fall of the [Berlin Wall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Wall "Berlin Wall") in November 2014.

In 2016, he was featured on the song "[A.I.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.I._(song) "A.I. (song)")" by American pop rock band [OneRepublic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OneRepublic "OneRepublic") from their fourth studio album _[Oh My My](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oh\_My\_My\_(album) "Oh My My (album)")_.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-94)[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-95)[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-96) In June, Gabriel released the single "I'm Amazing". The song was written several years prior, in part as a tribute to boxer [Muhammad Ali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muhammad_Ali "Muhammad Ali").[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-97) That month, he embarked on a joint tour with [Sting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sting_(musician) "Sting (musician)") titled _The Rock Paper Scissors North American Tour_.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-98)

Gabriel re-emerged in 2019 with the release of _[Rated PG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rated\_PG\_(Peter\_Gabriel\_album) "Rated PG (Peter Gabriel album)")_, a compilation of songs that were created for film soundtracks throughout his career. The song selection spans over 30 years and includes tracks that had never been released on an official Gabriel album previously, including "[Down to Earth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Down_to_Earth_(Peter_Gabriel_song) "Down to Earth (Peter Gabriel song)")" (from _[WALL-E](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WALL-E\_(soundtrack) "WALL-E (soundtrack)")_) and "That'll Do" (from _[Babe: Pig in the City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babe:\_Pig\_in\_the\_City#Soundtrack "Babe: Pig in the City")_), an Oscar-nominated collaboration with [Randy Newman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randy_Newman "Randy Newman"). Initially only released on vinyl for [Record Store Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Record_Store_Day "Record Store Day") on 13 April, the album was eventually released on digital streaming services later that month.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-99) Later that same year, Gabriel issued another digital release on 13 September titled _[Flotsam and Jetsam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flotsam\_and\_Jetsam\_(Peter\_Gabriel\_album) "Flotsam and Jetsam (Peter Gabriel album)")_, a collection of [B-sides](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B-side "B-side"), remixes and rarities that span Gabriel's entire solo career from 1976 to 2016, including his first solo recording, a cover of [the Beatles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles "The Beatles")' song "[Strawberry Fields Forever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strawberry_Fields_Forever "Strawberry Fields Forever")".[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-100)

### 2022–present: _I/O_ and _O\I_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Peter_Gabriel&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 2022–present: I/O and O\I")]

By 2002, Gabriel had been continually working on what he had given the tentative title of _[I/O](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I/O\_(album) "I/O (album)")_, his tenth studio album, which he had begun work on as early as 1995.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-101)[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-102) It was originally set to be released 18 months after _Up_, but touring pushed the release far away.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-103) He did an interview with _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ in 2005 stating that he had 150 songs in various stages.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-104) From 2013 to 2016, he posted regularly on social media about recording the new album.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-105) In 2019, he spoke on [BBC Radio 6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Radio_6_Music "BBC Radio 6 Music") about how he had taken a hiatus from making music due to his wife being sick, but he had begun to return to it now that she had recovered.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-106) In 2021, he was interviewed multiple times about his new album, and revealed that he had been recording with [Manu Katché](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manu_Katch%C3%A9 "Manu Katché"), [Tony Levin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Levin "Tony Levin") and [David Rhodes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Rhodes_(guitarist) "David Rhodes (guitarist)") on 17 new songs.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-107)[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-108) He posted multiple photos to his Facebook and Instagram of these sessions.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-109)[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-110) In June 2022, Katché told the French magazine _[L'Illustré](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L'Illustr%C3%A9 "L'Illustré")_ that the album was nearly complete and would be released later that year, pending an official announcement.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-111)[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-112)[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-113)

In November 2022, Gabriel announced his upcoming [I/O The Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I/O_The_Tour "I/O The Tour") for the spring of 2023 across several European cities, with later dates to be confirmed for the North America leg of the tour for the late summer/fall of 2023.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-114) This announcement also confirmed the name of the upcoming album to be stylised as _I/O_. The first single from the album, "[Panopticom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panopticom "Panopticom")", was released digitally on 6 January 2023.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-115) A new piece from the album was released on the date of each full moon in 2023,[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-116) as well as a different mix of the song on each new moon in 2023, starting with the Dark Side Mix of "Panopticom".[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-117) On 5 February, Gabriel released "[The Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Court_(song) "The Court (song)")", the second single from the album. On 7 March, Gabriel released the third single, "[Playing for Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Playing_for_Time_(song) "Playing for Time (song)")". A basic arrangement of the song featuring only Gabriel on piano and Levin on bass had already opened the shows on the [Back to Front Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Back_to_Front_Tour "Back to Front Tour"), by the name of "Daddy Long Legs".[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-118)[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-119) The title track "[I/O](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I/O_(song) "I/O (song)")" was the fourth single released on 6 April. On 5 May, Peter Gabriel released the fifth single from the album, "[Four Kinds of Horses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Four_Kinds_of_Horses "Four Kinds of Horses")", a track which is a collaboration with [Brian Eno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Eno "Brian Eno") and [Richard Russell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Russell_(record_producer) "Richard Russell (record producer)"). The sixth single, "[Road to Joy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_to_Joy_(Peter_Gabriel_song) "Road to Joy (Peter Gabriel song)")", was released on 4 June. Six more singles were released, separately, within the next six months—"[So Much](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/So_Much_(Peter_Gabriel_song) "So Much (Peter Gabriel song)")", "[Olive Tree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olive_Tree_(song) "Olive Tree (song)")", "[Love Can Heal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love_Can_Heal "Love Can Heal")", "[This Is Home](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/This_Is_Home_(Peter_Gabriel_song) "This Is Home (Peter Gabriel song)")", "[And Still](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/And_Still_(Peter_Gabriel_song) "And Still (Peter Gabriel song)")" and "[Live and Let Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_and_Let_Live_(Peter_Gabriel_song) "Live and Let Live (Peter Gabriel song)")"—before _I/O_ was finally released on 1 December 2023.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-120)

One day prior to _I/O_'s release, Gabriel told _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_ that he did not expect a follow-up album (which he described as his "brain project") to take another 21 years, saying that "there's a lot of stuff in the can" but added that the material was not yet finished.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-121)

Additionally, Gabriel stated in his November 2023 Full Moon update video that the track "What Lies Ahead" will be on "the next record".[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-122) He performed "What Lies Ahead" several times in 2023 and it was a contender for _I/O_. In February 2025, Gabriel revealed to _[Mojo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mojo\_(magazine) "Mojo (magazine)")_ that he was working on the follow-up to _I/O_: "It will be called _O/I_ [...] that's _I/O_ backwards."[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-123) The first song from _[O\I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/O%5CI "O\I")_, "[Been Undone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Been_Undone "Been Undone")", was released on streaming platforms on 3 January 2026. Gabriel will continue releasing songs from the project on days that correlate to the [full moon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Full_moon "Full moon").[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-124)[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-125)

## Artistry

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Peter_Gabriel&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Artistry")]

Stylistically, Gabriel's music has been variously described as [progressive rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progressive_rock "Progressive rock"),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-hudak-1)[art rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_rock "Art rock"),[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-So_%E2%80%93_Peter_Gabriel_(review)-126)[art pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_pop "Art pop"),[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-127)[pop rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_rock "Pop rock"),[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-128)[worldbeat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Worldbeat "Worldbeat"),[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-129)[post-progressive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-progressive "Post-progressive"),[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-130) and [progressive soul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progressive_soul "Progressive soul").[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-FOOTNOTEEaslea201818:_The_Tremble_in_the_Hips:_''So''-131) According to _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ journalist Ryan Reed, Gabriel has developed in all as an "art-rock innovator, soul-pop craftsman, [and] 'world music' ambassador" over the course of his career,[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-132) while music scholar Gregg Akkermann argues that, despite his progressive rock origins, he has "managed to attract fans from across the spectrum: prog rock, alternative rock, world beat, blue-eyed soul, dance music, the college crowd, the teens, Americans and Europeans".[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-133) More broadly, [AllMusic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AllMusic "AllMusic")'s [Stephen Thomas Erlewine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Thomas_Erlewine "Stephen Thomas Erlewine") says Gabriel emerged during the 1980s as "one of rock's most ambitious, innovative musicians", as well as "an international pop star".[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-134)

Gabriel has worked with a relatively stable crew of musicians and recording engineers throughout his solo career. Bass and [Stick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chapman_Stick "Chapman Stick") player [Tony Levin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Levin "Tony Levin") has performed on every Gabriel studio album and every live tour except for _Scratch My Back_ (2010), the soundtracks _Passion_ (1989) and _Long Walk Home_ (2002), and the New Blood Tour. Guitarist [David Rhodes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Rhodes_(guitarist) "David Rhodes (guitarist)") has been Gabriel's guitarist of choice since 1979. Prior to _So_ (1986), [Jerry Marotta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Marotta "Jerry Marotta") was Gabriel's preferred drummer, both in the studio and on the road. (For the _So_ and _Us_ albums and tours Marotta was replaced by [Manu Katché](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manu_Katch%C3%A9 "Manu Katché"), who was then replaced by [Ged Lynch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ged_Lynch "Ged Lynch") on parts of the _Up_ album and all of the subsequent tour). Gabriel is known for choosing top-flight collaborators, from co-producers such as Ezrin, Fripp, Lillywhite and Lanois to musicians such as [Natalie Merchant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natalie_Merchant "Natalie Merchant"), [Elizabeth Fraser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_Fraser "Elizabeth Fraser"), [L. Shankar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L._Shankar "L. Shankar"), [Trent Reznor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trent_Reznor "Trent Reznor"), [Youssou N'Dour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Youssou_N'Dour "Youssou N'Dour"), [Larry Fast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_Fast "Larry Fast"), [Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nusrat_Fateh_Ali_Khan "Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan"), [Sinéad O'Connor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sin%C3%A9ad_O'Connor "Sinéad O'Connor"), [Kate Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Bush "Kate Bush"), [Ane Brun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ane_Brun "Ane Brun"), [Paula Cole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Cole "Paula Cole"), [John Giblin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Giblin "John Giblin"), [Dave Gregory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Gregory_(musician) "Dave Gregory (musician)"), [Peter Hammill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Hammill "Peter Hammill"), [Papa Wemba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papa_Wemba "Papa Wemba"), [Manu Katché](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manu_Katch%C3%A9 "Manu Katché"), [Bayete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jabu_Khanyile "Jabu Khanyile"), [Milton Nascimento](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milton_Nascimento "Milton Nascimento"), [Phil Collins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phil_Collins "Phil Collins"), [Stewart Copeland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stewart_Copeland "Stewart Copeland") and [OneRepublic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OneRepublic "OneRepublic").

Over the years, Gabriel has collaborated with singer [Kate Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Bush "Kate Bush") several times; Bush provided backing vocals for Gabriel's "Games Without Frontiers" and "No Self Control" in 1980, and female lead vocal for "Don't Give Up" (a top 10 hit in the UK) in 1986, and Gabriel appeared on her television special. Their duet of [Roy Harper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Harper_(singer) "Roy Harper (singer)")'s "[Another Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Another_Day_(Roy_Harper_song) "Another Day (Roy Harper song)")" was discussed for release as a single, but never appeared.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-135)

He also collaborated with [avant-garde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avant-garde "Avant-garde") artist [Laurie Anderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurie_Anderson "Laurie Anderson") on two versions of her composition "[Excellent Birds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Excellent_Birds "Excellent Birds")"—one for her second album _[Mister Heartbreak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mister\_Heartbreak "Mister Heartbreak")_ (1984),[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-136) and another version called "[This is the Picture (Excellent Birds)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Excellent_Birds#Background "Excellent Birds")", which appeared on original [cassette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audio_cassette "Audio cassette") and CD versions, and all versions past 2002, of _So_.

Gabriel sang (along with [Jim Kerr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Kerr "Jim Kerr") of [Simple Minds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simple_Minds "Simple Minds")) on "Everywhere I Go", from [the Call](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Call_(band) "The Call (band)")'s 1986 studio album, _Reconciled_. On [Toni Childs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toni_Childs "Toni Childs")' 1994 studio album, _[The Woman's Boat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Woman's\_Boat "The Woman's Boat")_, Gabriel sang on the track, "I Met a Man".[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-137)

In 1998, Gabriel appeared on the soundtrack of _[Babe: Pig in the City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babe:\_Pig\_in\_the\_City "Babe: Pig in the City")_ as the lead vocalist of the song "That'll Do", written by [Randy Newman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randy_Newman "Randy Newman"). The song was nominated for an [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards"), and Gabriel and Newman performed it at the following year's Oscar telecast. He performed a similar soundtrack appearance for the 2004 film _[Shall We Dance?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shall\_We\_Dance%3F\_(2004\_film) "Shall We Dance? (2004 film)")_, singing a [cover version](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cover_version "Cover version") of "[The Book of Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Book_of_Love_(The_Magnetic_Fields_song) "The Book of Love (The Magnetic Fields song)")" by [the Magnetic Fields](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Magnetic_Fields "The Magnetic Fields").

In 1987, Gabriel appeared on [Robbie Robertson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robbie_Robertson "Robbie Robertson")'s [self-titled solo studio album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robbie_Robertson_(album) "Robbie Robertson (album)"), singing on "[Fallen Angel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallen_Angel_(Robbie_Robertson_song) "Fallen Angel (Robbie Robertson song)")"; co-wrote two [Tom Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Robinson "Tom Robinson") singles; and appeared on [Joni Mitchell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joni_Mitchell "Joni Mitchell")'s 1988 studio album _[Chalk Mark in a Rain Storm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chalk\_Mark\_in\_a\_Rain\_Storm "Chalk Mark in a Rain Storm")_, on the opening track "[My Secret Place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My_Secret_Place "My Secret Place")".

In 2001, Gabriel contributed lead vocals to the song "When You're Falling" on [Afro Celt Sound System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afro_Celt_Sound_System "Afro Celt Sound System")'s _[Volume 3: Further in Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volume\_3:\_Further\_in\_Time "Volume 3: Further in Time")_.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-138) In the summer of 2003, Gabriel performed in Ohio with a guest performance by Uzbek singer [Sevara Nazarkhan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevara_Nazarkhan "Sevara Nazarkhan").

Gabriel collaborated on tracks with electronic musician [BT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BT_(musician) "BT (musician)"), who also worked on the _OVO_ soundtrack with him. The tracks were never released, as the computers they were contained on were stolen from BT's home in California. He also sang the lyrics for [Deep Forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep_Forest "Deep Forest") on their theme song for the movie _[Strange Days](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strange\_Days\_(film) "Strange Days (film)")_ (1995). In addition, Gabriel has appeared on [Angelique Kidjo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angelique_Kidjo "Angelique Kidjo")'s 2007 studio album _[Djin Djin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Djin\_Djin "Djin Djin")_, singing on the song "Salala".

Gabriel has recorded a cover of the [Vampire Weekend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vampire_Weekend "Vampire Weekend") single "[Cape Cod Kwassa Kwassa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Cod_Kwassa_Kwassa "Cape Cod Kwassa Kwassa")" with [Hot Chip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_Chip "Hot Chip"), where his name is mentioned several times in the chorus. He substitutes the original line "But this feels so unnatural / Peter Gabriel too / This feels so unnatural/ Peter Gabriel too" with "It feels so unnatural / Peter Gabriel too / and it feels so unnatural / to sing your own name."[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-139)

Gabriel collaborated with [Arcade Fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcade_Fire "Arcade Fire") on their 2022 studio album, _[We](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We\_(Arcade\_Fire\_album) "We (Arcade Fire album)")_. He sang backing vocals on the track "Unconditional II (Race and Religion)".[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-140)

## WOMAD and other projects

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Peter_Gabriel&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: WOMAD and other projects")]

Gabriel's interest in [world music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_music "World music") was first apparent on his third solo studio album. According to Spencer Kornhaber in _[The Atlantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Atlantic "The Atlantic")_ in 2019: "When Peter Gabriel moved toward 'world music' four decades ago, he not only evangelized sounds that were novel to Western pop. He also set a radio template: majestic, with flourishes meant to read as 'exotic,' and lyrics meant to change lives."[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-141) This influence has increased over time, and he co-founded the [World of Music, Arts and Dance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_of_Music,_Arts_and_Dance "World of Music, Arts and Dance") (WOMAD) festival in 1982.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-Lynskey_2007-4) Gabriel said:

> The first time I really got into music from another culture was as a result of the shifting of [Radio 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Radio_4 "BBC Radio 4"), which I used to wake up to. I'd lost it on [medium wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medium_wave "Medium wave") and was groping around in the morning on the dial, trying to find something that I could listen to, and came across a Dutch radio station who were playing the soundtrack from some obscure [Stanley Baker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Baker "Stanley Baker") movie called _[Dingaka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dingaka "Dingaka")_. That had quite a lot of stuff from—I think it was—Ghana. I can't remember now, but it really moved me. One of the songs I heard on that was a thing called '[Shosholoza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shosholoza "Shosholoza")', which I recorded on the b-side of the '[Biko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biko_(song) "Biko (song)")' single.[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-142)

Gabriel created the [Real World Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_World_Studios "Real World Studios") and record label to facilitate the creation and distribution of such music by various artists, and he has worked to educate Western culture about such musicians as [Yungchen Lhamo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yungchen_Lhamo "Yungchen Lhamo"), [Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nusrat_Fateh_Ali_Khan "Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan") and [Youssou N'dour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Youssou_N'dour "Youssou N'dour").

In the 1990s, with Steve Nelson of Brilliant Media and director Michael Coulson, he developed advanced multimedia CD-ROM-based entertainment projects, creating _Xplora_ (the world's largest-selling music CD-ROM), and subsequently the _[EVE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter\_Gabriel:\_Eve "Peter Gabriel: Eve")_ CD-ROM. _EVE_ was a music and art adventure game directed by Michael Coulson and co-produced by the [Starwave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starwave "Starwave") Corporation in Seattle; it won the Milia d'Or award Grand Prize at the Cannes in 1996.

In 1990, Gabriel lent his backing vocals to Ugandan political exile [Geoffrey Oryema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoffrey_Oryema "Geoffrey Oryema")'s "Land of Anaka", appearing on Oryema's first studio album _Exile_, released on Gabriel's Real World label.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-143)

In 1994, Gabriel starred in [Breck Eisner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breck_Eisner "Breck Eisner")'s short film _Recon_ as a detective who enters the minds of murder victims to find their killer's identity.

Gabriel helped pioneer a new realm of musical interaction in 2001, visiting [Georgia State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_State_University "Georgia State University")'s Language Research Center to participate in keyboard jam sessions with [bonobo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonobo "Bonobo") apes from the Democratic Republic of the Congo. (This experience inspired the song "Animal Nation", which was performed on Gabriel's 2002 "Growing Up" tour and was featured on the _[Growing Up Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Growing\_Up\_Live "Growing Up Live")_ DVD and _[The Wild Thornberrys Movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Wild\_Thornberrys\_Movie "The Wild Thornberrys Movie")_ soundtrack.) Gabriel's desire to bring attention to the intelligence of primates also took the form of ApeNet, a project that aimed to link great apes through the internet, enabling the first interspecies internet communication.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-144)

Gabriel was one of the founders of on Demand Distribution ([OD2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OD2 "OD2")), one of the first online music download services. Prior to its closure in 2009, its technology had been used by over 100 music download sites including MSN Music UK, MyCokeMusic, Planet Internet (KPN), Wanadoo and CD WOW!. OD2 was bought by US company Loudeye in June 2004 and subsequently by Finnish mobile giant [Nokia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nokia "Nokia") in October 2006 for $60 million.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-145)

Gabriel is co-founder (with [Brian Eno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Eno "Brian Eno")) of a musicians union called Mudda, short for "magnificent union of digitally downloading artists".[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-146)[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-147)

In 2000, Gabriel collaborated with [Zucchero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zucchero "Zucchero"), [Anggun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anggun "Anggun") and others in a charity for kids with [AIDS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HIV/AIDS "HIV/AIDS"). Erick Benzi wrote words and music and Patrick Bruel, Stephan Eicher, Faudel, Lokua Kanza, Laam, Nourith, Axelle Red have accepted to sing it.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-148)

In 2003, Gabriel contributed a song for the video game _Uru: Ages Beyond Myst_.[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-149) In 2004, Gabriel contributed another song ("Curtains") and contributed voice work on another game in the [Myst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Myst "Myst") franchise, _[Myst IV: Revelation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Myst\_IV:\_Revelation "Myst IV: Revelation")_.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-150)

In June 2005, Gabriel and broadcast industry entrepreneur [David Engelke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Engelke "David Engelke") purchased [Solid State Logic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solid_State_Logic "Solid State Logic"), a manufacturer of mixing consoles and digital audio workstations.[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-151) In 2017, the company was sold to the [Audiotonix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audiotonix "Audiotonix") Group.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-152)
