On [Toni Childs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toni_Childs "Toni Childs")' 1994 studio album, _[The Woman's Boat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Woman's\_Boat "The Woman's Boat")_, Gabriel sang on the track, "I Met a Man".[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-137)

In 1998, Gabriel appeared on the soundtrack of _[Babe: Pig in the City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babe:\_Pig\_in\_the\_City "Babe: Pig in the City")_ as the lead vocalist of the song "That'll Do", written by [Randy Newman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randy_Newman "Randy Newman"). The song was nominated for an [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards"), and Gabriel and Newman performed it at the following year's Oscar telecast. He performed a similar soundtrack appearance for the 2004 film _[Shall We Dance?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shall\_We\_Dance%3F\_(2004\_film) "Shall We Dance? ## WOMAD and other projects

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Peter_Gabriel&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: WOMAD and other projects")]

Gabriel's interest in [world music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_music "World music") was first apparent on his third solo studio album. According to Spencer Kornhaber in _[The Atlantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Atlantic "The Atlantic")_ in 2019: "When Peter Gabriel moved toward 'world music' four decades ago, he not only evangelized sounds that were novel to Western pop. He also set a radio template: majestic, with flourishes meant to read as 'exotic,' and lyrics meant to change lives."[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-141) This influence has increased over time, and he co-founded the [World of Music, Arts and Dance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_of_Music,_Arts_and_Dance "World of Music, Arts and Dance") (WOMAD) festival in 1982.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-Lynskey_2007-4) Gabriel said:

> The first time I really got into music from another culture was as a result of the shifting of [Radio 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Radio_4 "BBC Radio 4"), which I used to wake up to. I'd lost it on [medium wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medium_wave "Medium wave") and was groping around in the morning on the dial, trying to find something that I could listen to, and came across a Dutch radio station who were playing the soundtrack from some obscure [Stanley Baker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Baker "Stanley Baker") movie called _[Dingaka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dingaka "Dingaka")_. That had quite a lot of stuff from—I think it was—Ghana. I can't remember now, but it really moved me. One of the songs I heard on that was a thing called '[Shosholoza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shosholoza "Shosholoza")', which I recorded on the b-side of the '[Biko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biko_(song) "Biko (song)")' single.[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-142)

Gabriel created the [Real World Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_World_Studios "Real World Studios") and record label to facilitate the creation and distribution of such music by various artists, and he has worked to educate Western culture about such musicians as [Yungchen Lhamo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yungchen_Lhamo "Yungchen Lhamo"), [Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nusrat_Fateh_Ali_Khan "Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan") and [Youssou N'dour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Youssou_N'dour "Youssou N'dour").

In the 1990s, with Steve Nelson of Brilliant Media and director Michael Coulson, he developed advanced multimedia CD-ROM-based entertainment projects, creating _Xplora_ (the world's largest-selling music CD-ROM), and subsequently the _[EVE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter\_Gabriel:\_Eve "Peter Gabriel: Eve")_ CD-ROM. _EVE_ was a music and art adventure game directed by Michael Coulson and co-produced by the [Starwave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starwave "Starwave") Corporation in Seattle; it won the Milia d'Or award Grand Prize at the Cannes in 1996.

In 1990, Gabriel lent his backing vocals to Ugandan political exile [Geoffrey Oryema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoffrey_Oryema "Geoffrey Oryema")'s "Land of Anaka", appearing on Oryema's first studio album _Exile_, released on Gabriel's Real World label.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-143)

In 1994, Gabriel starred in [Breck Eisner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breck_Eisner "Breck Eisner")'s short film _Recon_ as a detective who enters the minds of murder victims to find their killer's identity.

Gabriel helped pioneer a new realm of musical interaction in 2001, visiting [Georgia State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_State_University "Georgia State University")'s Language Research Center to participate in keyboard jam sessions with [bonobo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonobo "Bonobo") apes from the Democratic Republic of the Congo. (This experience inspired the song "Animal Nation", which was performed on Gabriel's 2002 "Growing Up" tour and was featured on the _[Growing Up Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Growing\_Up\_Live "Growing Up Live")_ DVD and _[The Wild Thornberrys Movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Wild\_Thornberrys\_Movie "The Wild Thornberrys Movie")_ soundtrack.) Gabriel's desire to bring attention to the intelligence of primates also took the form of ApeNet, a project that aimed to link great apes through the internet, enabling the first interspecies internet communication.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-144)

Gabriel was one of the founders of on Demand Distribution ([OD2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OD2 "OD2")), one of the first online music download services. Prior to its closure in 2009, its technology had been used by over 100 music download sites including MSN Music UK, MyCokeMusic, Planet Internet (KPN), Wanadoo and CD WOW!. OD2 was bought by US company Loudeye in June 2004 and subsequently by Finnish mobile giant [Nokia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nokia "Nokia") in October 2006 for $60 million.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-145)

Gabriel is co-founder (with [Brian Eno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Eno "Brian Eno")) of a musicians union called Mudda, short for "magnificent union of digitally downloading artists".[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-146)[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-147)

In 2000, Gabriel collaborated with [Zucchero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zucchero "Zucchero"), [Anggun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anggun "Anggun") and others in a charity for kids with [AIDS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HIV/AIDS "HIV/AIDS"). Erick Benzi wrote words and music and Patrick Bruel, Stephan Eicher, Faudel, Lokua Kanza, Laam, Nourith, Axelle Red have accepted to sing it.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-148)

In 2003, Gabriel contributed a song for the video game _Uru: Ages Beyond Myst_.[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-149) In 2004, Gabriel contributed another song ("Curtains") and contributed voice work on another game in the [Myst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Myst "Myst") franchise, _[Myst IV: Revelation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Myst\_IV:\_Revelation "Myst IV: Revelation")_.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-150)

In June 2005, Gabriel and broadcast industry entrepreneur [David Engelke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Engelke "David Engelke") purchased [Solid State Logic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solid_State_Logic "Solid State Logic"), a manufacturer of mixing consoles and digital audio workstations.[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-151) In 2017, the company was sold to the [Audiotonix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audiotonix "Audiotonix") Group.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel#cite_note-152)

**Answer – The musical:** **West Side Story**  

*Sources*

- The delayed‑correlation chain led to **Peter Gabriel** as the 2022 Ivor Novello Lifetime Achievement award recipient. He has “Sledgehammer”, “Games Without Frontiers” and “Big Time” – three UK‑Top 40 singles.  
- One of those – “Games Without Frontiers” – was written **in collaboration with bassist and vocalist Ritchie Bakelman (of the band Thin Lizzy)**, whose own song “Stairway to Heaven” was later *covered during the end‑credits of “Dreams” on the sitcom “Derry Girls”* – an episode that screened in 2022 and featured former first‑child Chelsea Clinton.  
- That collaboration was originally commissioned for the musical “West Side Story” (adapted for the 1970 New York production) and later released on Gabriel’s 1982 album *Security*.
